title: 2020 AMC 10A Problem 20
statement: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) satisfies \(\angle ABC = \angle ACD = 90^{\circ},\) \(AC=20,\) and \(CD=30.\) Diagonals \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{BD}\) intersect at point \(E,\) and \(AE=5.\) What is the area of quadrilateral \(ABCD?\)

solutions.text:
Place \(A=(0,0)\) and \(C=(20,0)\). Since \(\angle ACD=90^\circ\) and \(CD=30\), take \(D=(20,30)\). The point \(E\) is \((5,0)\), so line \(BD\) has equation \(y=2(x-5)\).

Because \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\), point \(B\) lies on the circle with diameter \(AC\): \((x-10)^2+y^2=100\). Intersecting with \(y=2(x-5)\) gives \(x=2\) or \(10\). The convex quadrilateral uses \(B=(2,-6)\).

Then \([ACD]=\dfrac12\cdot20\cdot30=300\), and \([ABC]=\dfrac12\cdot20\cdot6=60\). The total area is \(360\). Thus, D is the correct answer.
